fills.fill: that is set above this world
fills.notes: The correspondential sequence defines the sun as a liminal vessel: a ‘gate of life’ and ‘vessel of peace’ belonging to the great aeon of Light yet appearing to the world below. A short locative clause is required to mark its placement as an upper boundary between aeon and cosmos, preparing the later language of ‘departure of souls’ and Satan’s interdiction.

The syntax requires a verbal complement: ‘There are five archetypes occur in the sun, it making them ___ as it finds the world.’ In the oldest cosmological register the sun does not ‘teach’ but ‘shows/displays/manifests’ forms; this matches the repeated ‘display/manifest’ used for both sun and night as signs of their essences.
Restores the vocative demonstrative opening that frames the teaching as a disclosure of correspondential ‘mysteries’ in day/night.

The sentence contrasts two genera by correspondence: those who are ‘children of day/light’ versus those who ‘bear’ (i.e., carry/embody in life) the character of Darkness. A participial/relative clause is demanded before ‘the character of the darkness’ to mark reception and embodiment rather than moral accusation, consistent with the impersonal substrate.

assessment: Most gaps are tightly constrained by repeated formulae (‘display/manifest’, ‘behold’) and by the correspondential structure (sun/night as signs of their prior essences). ¶2 and ¶37 allow more than one equivalent phrasing, but the required function (upper limen of the light-aeon; embodiment of the darkness-character) narrows the restorations to a small semantic range.
